D000787.s: The symptom of paroxysmal pain consequent to myocardial ischemia usually of distinctive character, location and radiation. It is thought to be provoked by a transient stressful situation during which the oxygen requirements of the myocardium exceed that supplied by the coronary circulation.

D001177.s: Chronic progressive degeneration of the stress-bearing portion of a joint, with bizarre hypertrophic changes at the periphery.

D003153.s: Diagnostic, therapeutic and preventive health services provided for individuals in the community.

D003247.s: The protection, preservation, restoration, and rational use of all resources in the total environment.

D003768.s: Contact between opposing teeth during a person's habitual bite.

D004332.s: Death that occurs as a result of anoxia or heart arrest, associated with immersion in liquid.

D004453.s: Use of reflected ultrasound in the diagnosis of intracranial pathologic processes.

D004538.s: A visual image which is recalled in accurate detail. It is a sort of projection of an image on a mental screen.

D004804.s: Granular leukocytes with a nucleus that usually has two lobes connected by a slender thread of chromatin, and cytoplasm containing coarse, round granules that are uniform in size and stainable by eosin.

D005331.s: Transplacental passage of fetal blood into the circulation of the maternal organism. (Dorland, 27th ed)

D005407.s: A whiplike motility appendage present on the surface cells. Prokaryote flagella are composed of a protein called flagellin. Bacteria can have a single flagellum, a tuft at one pole, or multiple flagella covering the entire surface.

D005490.s: An infection at a specific location that may spread to another region of the body.

D005779.s: Technique involving the diffusion of antigen or antibody through a semisolid medium, usually agar or agarose gel, with the result being a precipitin reaction.

D005793.s: The phenomenon of an organism's responding to all situations similar to one in which it has been conditioned.

D006015.s: An x-linked recessive hepatic glycogen storage disease resulting from lack of expression of phosphorylase-b-kinase activity. Symptoms are relatively mild; hepatomegaly, increased liver glycogen, and decreased leukocyte phosphorylase are present. Liver shrinkage occurs in response to glucagon.

D006745.s: The number of beds from 300 to 499 which a hospital has been designed and constructed to contain. It may also refer to the number of beds set up and staffed for use.

D007034.s: The part of the hypothalamus posterior to the middle region consisting of several nuclei including the medial maxillary nucleus, lateral mammillary nucleus, and posterior hypothalamic nucleus (posterior hypothalamic area).

D008677.s: The phase of cell nucleus division following prometaphase, in which the chromosomes line up across the equatorial plane of the spindle apparatus prior to separation.

D008800.s: A country in north america, bordering the Caribbean Sea and the gulf of america, between belize and the united states, and bordering the North Pacific Ocean, between Guatemala and the united states.

D009313.s: Components of a national health care system which administer specific services, e.g., national health insurance.

D009502.s: Electrically neutral elementary particles found in all atomic nuclei except light hydrogen; the mass is equal to that of the proton and electron combined and they are unstable when isolated from the nucleus, undergoing beta decay.

D010535.s: A procedure in which a laparoscope (laparoscopes) is inserted through a small incision near the navel to examine the abdominal and pelvic organs in the peritoneal cavity. If appropriate, biopsy or surgery can be performed during laparoscopy.

D011301.s: Region of hypothalamus between the anterior commissure and optic chiasm.

D011640.s: A course or method of action selected, usually by a government, from among alternatives to guide and determine present and future decisions.

D011749.s: Substances capable of increasing body temperature and cause fever and may be used for fever therapy. They may be of microbial origin, often polysaccharides, and may contaminate distilled water.

D012018.s: An involuntary movement or exercise of function in a part, excited in response to a stimulus applied to the periphery and transmitted to the brain or spinal cord.

D012133.s: Complete or severe weakness of the muscles of respiration. This condition may be associated with motor neuron diseases; peripheral nerve diseases; neuromuscular junction diseases; spinal cord diseases; injury to the phrenic nerve; and other disorders.

D012689.s: The sequential correspondence of nucleotides in one nucleic acid molecule with those of another nucleic acid molecule. Sequence homology is an indication of the genetic relatedness of different organisms and gene function.

D012780.s: The use of focused short radio waves to produce local hyperthermia in an injured person or diseased body area.

D014566.s: All the organs involved in reproduction and the formation and release of urine. It includes the kidneys, ureters, bladder; urethra, and the organs of reproduction - ovaries, uterus; fallopian tubes; vagina; and clitoris in women and the testes; seminal vesicles; prostate; seminal ducts; and penis…

D014805.s: A cobalt-containing coordination compound produced by intestinal micro-organisms and found also in soil and water. Higher plants do not concentrate vitamin B 12 from the soil and so are a poor source of the substance as compared with animal tissues.

D015895.s: Coded listings of physician or other professional services using units that indicate the relative value of the various services they perform. They take into account time, skill, and overhead cost required for each service, but generally do not consider the relative cost-effectiveness.

D015921.s: Biocompatible materials placed into (endosseous) or onto (subperiosteal) the jawbone to support a crown, bridge, or artificial tooth, or to stabilize a diseased tooth.

D016726.s: A tumor-like inflammatory lesion of the lung that is composed of plasma cells and fibrous tissue. It is also known as an inflammatory pseudotumor, often with calcification and measuring between 2 and 5 cm in diameter.

e: Myoclonus Progressive Epilepsy of Unverricht and Lundborg
Myoclonic Epilepsy of Unverricht and Lundborg
D020194.s: An autosomal recessive condition characterized by recurrent myoclonic and generalized seizures, ataxia, slowly progressive intellectual deterioration, dysarthria, and intention tremor. Myoclonic seizures are severe and continuous, and tend to be triggered by movement, stress, and sensory stimuli.

D020330.s: A syndrome characterized by the acute onset of unilateral facial paralysis which progresses over a 2-5 day period. Weakness of the orbicularis oculi muscle and resulting incomplete eye closure may be associated with corneal injury. Pain behind the ear often precedes the onset of paralysis.

D020460.s: Melanin-containing organelles found in melanocytes and melanophores.

D020529.s: The most common clinical variant of multiple sclerosis, characterized by recurrent acute exacerbations of neurologic dysfunction followed by partial or complete recovery. Common clinical manifestations include loss of visual (see optic neuritis), motor, sensory, or bladder function.

D027641.s: Therapeutic use of humor and laughter to improve emotional well being and health.

e: Deafness, Congenital, and Functional Heart Disease
Prolonged QT Interval in EKG and Sudden Death
Cardioauditory Syndrome of Jervell and Lange-Nielsen
D029593.s: A form of long QT syndrome that is associated with congenital deafness. It is characterized by abnormal cardioelectrophysiology involving the voltage-gated potassium channel. It results from mutation of KCNQ1 gene (Subtype 1 or JLN1) or the KCNE1 gene (Subtype 2 or JLN2).

D031941.s: A systemic infection of various salmonid and a few nonsalmonid fishes caused by Viral hemorrhagic septicemia virus (see novirhabdovirus),

D034582.s: The outer covering of the body composed of the SKIN and the skin appendages, which are the HAIR, the nails; and the sebaceous glands and the sweat glands and their ducts.

D054908.s: Tuberculosis resistant to isoniazid and rifampin and at least three of the six main classes of second-line drugs (aminoglycosides; polypeptide agents; fluoroquinolones; thioamides; cycloserine; and PARA-aminosalicylic acid) as defined by the CDC.

e: Small Cell Cancer Of The Lung
D055752.s: A form of highly malignant lung cancer that is composed of small ovoid cells (small cell carcinoma).

D056656.s: Microdevices that combine microfluidics technology with electrical and/or mechanical functions for analyzing very small fluid volumes. They consist of microchannels etched into substrates made of silicon, glass, or polymer using processes similar to photolithography.

D058113.s: Compounds that disintegrate natural waxy exudates such as ear wax.

D059411.s: Symptoms of disorders of the lower urinary tract including frequency, nocturia; urgency, incomplete voiding, and urinary incontinence. They are often associated with overactive bladder; urinary incompetence; and interstitial cystitis.

D061805.s: The lengthening of a nascent RNA molecule by rna polymerase during transcription.

D063726.s: A delusional disorder of belief in infestation by insects or other parasites. This formication is typically accompanied by dermatological manifestation such as pruritus that may lead to self-mutilation in order to remove the perceived parasites.

D064424.s: Use of tobacco (Nicotiana tabacum L) and tobacco products.

D064749.s: A rare congenital abnormality resulting in the ureter passing dorsal to and being obstructed by the inferior vena cava.

D000079763.s: Procedures with non-continuous blood purification (e.g., dialysis, filtration and/or perfusion) via vascular access by increasing blood flow rate compared to continuous rrt.

D000080345.s: A group of inherited disorders characterized by incomplete development of the retinal vasculature. Its severity can vary from complete blindness in infancy, to mild or no visual problems, where small areas of vascular defects are observable only by fluorescein angiography.

D000088082.s: Beverages that are prepared by using microorganisms to convert their components into various fermentation end products.

D000094384.s: Ability of the innate immunity system to form immunologic memory and provide enhanced defense against subsequent secondary infections.

D000096724.s: Infectious diseases transmitted by mosquito vectors. Mosquito-borne human viral diseases include Chikungunya, Dengue, viral encephalitis (e.g., Japanese and St. Louis types), West Nile, Yellow fever, Zika virus infections.
